To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

hexose-6 phosphate dehydrogenase, a microsomal NADP(H) regenerating enzyme, is a key regulator of the redox state of the endoplasmatic reticulum, thereby controlling 11beta-hyroxy steroid dehydrogenase 1, the enzyme that activates glucocorticoid hormones.

the redox status of the endoplasmatic reticulum is a key determinant for 11beta-hyroxy steroid dehydrogenase 1 (11 beta-HSD1) oxo-reductive activity, and that hexose-6- phosphate dehydrogenase, a NADP+-reducing enzyme, is a key determinant of this redox status.

hexose-6- phosphate dehydrogenase, a microsomal NADPH-generating system, cooperates with 11beta-hy-droxysteroid dehydro-genase type 1, a bidirectional microsomal enzyme, to determine the intracellular availability of glucocorticosteroid hormones.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of H6PDH regulation, the functional cooperation of H6PDh with 11beta-HD1 and its potential as a novel target in the treatment of insulin resistance and the related metabolic syndrome.
elucidating the role of the H6PDH-11beta-HSD system for the prereceptor regulation of glucocorticosteroid availability.
the role of H6PDH in the control of 11beta-HSHD1 activity and the regulation of glucocorticosteroid metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of H6PDH in the control of 11beta-HDS1 activity has not been fully elucidated.
H6PD is not a prerequisite for 11beta-HDS1 activity, but that it can be an important modulator of the activity of 11beta-HS1, especially under conditions of oxidative stress.
H6PDG and 11betaHSD1 cooperate in a functional redox cycle in vivo, but the physiological relevance of this cooperation has to be established.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
H6PDG and 11betaHSD1 cooperate to maintain intracellular redox balance and to control intracellular glucocorticoid levels.
the redox status of the endoplasmatic reticulum is a key factor in determining 11beta-HDS1 activity and thus glucocorticoid activation.

H6PD is a key enzyme in the control of 11beta-HS activity, and that the regulation of 11betaHSD1 activity by H6PD is likely to play a significant role in the control of intracellular glucocorticoid levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intracellular redox state is an important regulator of glucocorticoidal activity.
the redox control of the 11beta-Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase type-1 activity is a complex mechanism that is not fully understood.
11beta-HOD1 and H6PDH form a functional unit in the endoplasmatic reticulum of cells and that the redox balance between these two enzymes is critical to the regulation of glucocorticiod availability.
